newsitem.title: ISRAEL: China vice-premier expresses confidence in Jiang.
newsitem.headline: China vice-premier expresses confidence in Jiang.

text.p: Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing, on a visit to Israel, expressed confidence on Thursday in the leadership of state President Jiang Zemin, the chosen heir to Deng Xiaoping.

"Under the third generation leadership of China with Mr Jiang Zemin at the core, the Chinese people and government are making great achievements along the path designed by Mr Deng Xiaoping," Li said through an interpreter after meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"During the eighties we doubled our economic output within a period of 10 years and during the first half of the 1990s in a period of five years we have been able to double our economy...
"This fully demonstrates the competence and abilities of the current Chinese leadership with Mr Jiang Zemin at the core," Li said.

Jiang, 70, is the chosen successor to Deng, who died on Wednesday at the age of 92. The only hint that the mantle of supreme authority had passed to the former tractor factory manager was an announcement that Jiang would head a 459-strong funeral committee.
In 1992, China -- eager to play a Middle East peace role -- became the last of the U.N. Security Council's five permanent members to establish ties with Israel.
Expressing his condolences to Li, Netanyahu praised Deng and called him "one of the great leaders of the 20th century".
Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor told Reuters that Li, who arrived in Israel on Sunday, would leave the country later on Thursday. Li had originally been set to head home on Friday.
